note: The Rulebook — follow these every time you make a short. AI-generated from our data + research; the AI adds/updates rules as we learn. Re-scanned Jun 2026 (38 own videos + 99 competitor scripts) and adversarially stress-tested every candidate — only effects that survive confound-checks become rules. Trust: ✅ validated = holds out-of-sample (LOO) · 🟡 directional = real but small-n/unproven · 🔵 craft = sound judgment, not yet in the stats.

stages.title: The intro — wins the SWIPE
stages.sub: Decided in ~1 second. The opening VISUAL is everything; words barely matter here.

stages.title: The body — wins WATCH-THROUGH (AVD)
stages.sub: What keeps them after the swipe. Audio + pacing + script.

stages.title: Topic — wins VIEWS
stages.sub: Views = topic + reach + luck, NOT opening craft.

stages.title: Craft notes
stages.sub: Sound practice that hasn't earned a coefficient yet.

stages.title: Testing queue — NOT rules yet
stages.sub: Re-scan (Jun 2026, n=38) checked these; none survived confound-checks. Vary ONE per upload so we can confirm or kill them.

stages.title: Confirmed non-levers — don't chase
stages.sub: These looked predictive but are confounds. Ignore them.

rules.rule: Every intro MUST have all four

items.label: Something INTERESTING / novel — a "what is that?!" mystery

rules.why: These are the four levers that stop the scroll. A face is validated (ρ+0.78); contrast is craft; early action and a novel/mysterious subject are directional. If an opening is missing any one, fix it before anything else.

rules.rule: Put a clear FACE in the first frame.
rules.why: Strongest swipe driver: ρ+0.78 (short bucket, n=11). Shorts with a face in frame 1 average ~74% stayed vs ~63% without.

rules.rule: Open on a MYSTERY — let them wonder "what is that?" Don't explain or label the object up front.
rules.why: Low object-clarity drives the swipe (ρ−0.73). Counter-example we caught: the floating-pot version with the plant already in it explained the object and scored lower than the bare floating pot.

rules.rule: Lead frame 1 with the cool thing ALREADY happening (the float, the glow, the arc) — never an inert/off object or a slow setup.
rules.why: The plasma re-edit gained +12.6 pts stayed by opening on the glowing ball instead of the off one. Put the payoff on frame 1.

rules.rule: Use quick CUTS in the first 4s (3+), and land the first cut/zoom before 0.5s — no static first second.
rules.why: Cuts in the first 4s: ρ+0.65. A slow/static opening second is a stall risk that bleeds the swipe.

rules.rule: NEVER narrate a "nothing's happening" / "it seems like nothing happens" line in the open.
rules.why: The clearest swipe-killer in the words analysis — and the 100-video competitor set agrees: top openings have ~0% dead-air.

rules.rule: Open LOUD and energetic — and NEVER ramp the loudness UP later.
rules.why: The AVD model: AVD ≈ 90.25 − 134·audio_buildup. Front-loaded loudness wins; ramping up tanks watch-through. (±2.1, most reliable model we have.)

rules.rule: Lean toward a STATEMENT over a question (a lean, not a law).
rules.why: Switching the phone-AC open from a question to a statement was a real win for THAT video. But honesty check: across our 38 videos, question-openers actually scored slightly HIGHER on swipe, and the competitor 'statement > question' gap (5.8M vs 2.9M views) is reach/length, not craft. So prefer statements, but it's unconfirmed.

rules.rule: Anchor the open on SURPRISE or a price ("I thought… but…", "$100") — keep stakes LOW, not tense.
rules.why: The floating-pot '$100 / I thought it was just two magnets' hook beat the dry explainer. But the re-scan found opening with heavy STAKES/tension tracked LOWER swipe in our data (and we over-use stakes: 3.4 vs competitors' 2.5). So anchor on surprise/price, not danger/tension. See the Testing queue.

rules.rule: Keep it SHORT — the shortest length that lands the hook + one clear payoff (single-object demo ≈ 20–25s).
rules.why: Shortening a 38s cut to ~22s lifted AVD. Rules differ by length bucket; short videos retain best.

rules.rule: To grow VIEWS, choose the FORMAT/topic — comparison/versus & knockoff tests beat single-object demos.
rules.why: Topic sets the view ceiling (our long-held finding). On 100 competitors, 'versus' formats out-viewed single-object demos massively — but that sample is small (n=6 versus) and reach-confounded, so treat the size of the gap loosely. Direction is solid; magnitude isn't.

rules.rule: Don't expect a better intro to grow VIEWS — opening craft drives the SWIPE and watch-through, not views.
rules.why: No opening/script feature predicts views (ours or 100 competitors'). Views = topic + channel reach + luck.

rules.rule: Keep it bright & high-contrast.
rules.why: Competitor top-view openings are brighter & clearer, but brightness isn't a proven swipe lever in our own data — treat as craft, don't over-tweak.

rules.rule: POST MORE and log swipe/AVD — that's the #1 way to sharpen predictions.
rules.why: At n=38 videos almost every effect is too small or too length/topic-confounded to confirm. More labeled videos > more analysis of the current 38, and > more competitor scraping (competitors can't validate engagement).

rules.rule: TEST: open with a superlative/extreme claim ("the illegal…", "the craziest…").
rules.why: It nudged BOTH our swipe (ρ=+0.29, p=.08) and competitor views (ρ=+0.29) — the only pattern that showed in both datasets. But only 6–7 of our videos use it and they cluster in long videos, so it failed the confound-check. Promising enough to A/B.

rules.rule: TEST: try LOWER-stakes, more-curious openings instead of tense/high-stakes ones.
rules.why: Our high-stakes opens correlate with LOWER swipe (ρ=−0.40; −0.63 in long videos), and we over-use stakes. Most interesting lead in the re-scan — but it's confounded by length/topic and a recompute softened it to −0.32, so it's a hypothesis, not a rule.

rules.rule: TEST (short videos only): slow the voiceover slightly.
rules.why: In short videos, faster talking tracked LOWER watch-through (ρ=−0.80) — but n=11 and outlier-driven, and the sign flips in long videos. Worth a deliberate test on short videos.

rules.rule: 'Fewer words → higher AVD' is NOT a lever.
rules.why: It's just video length. ρ=−0.46 overall but the sign FLIPS to +0.40 inside the long bucket — classic length confound. Don't cut words to chase AVD.

rules.rule: 'Add a CTA → more views' is NOT a lever.
rules.why: It's channel size. ρ=+0.43 overall, but within Hafu Go it's +0.03 and within Disobey Normal it's −0.22 (sign flip). Big channels add CTAs and already have reach — the CTA isn't buying the views.

rules.rule: Competitor VIEW patterns are an idea bank, not a rulebook.
rules.why: Format, superlatives, statements, slow pace all correlate with competitor views — but views = reach + topic + channel size, and competitors have NO swipe/AVD, so none of it can prove an engagement lever. Mine the Competitors tab for ideas to TEST, never as proof.
